findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so this bucket (which receives the vendor roster object) has no configuration-enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption.

Unlike the sibling buckets, no ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so there is no explicit private access boundary and nothing prevents a later public ACL or bucket policy grant on a bucket holding vendor data.

No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket is not recorded, preventing detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access. Note the sibling model_artifacts bucket does log to audit_trail, indicating logging is the intended pattern here.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial export data is stored without configuration-enforced default server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads and writes of financial ledger export data are not audited.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to this financial-data bucket, so the private ACL is the only barrier and a later public ACL or policy grant would not be blocked as defence in depth.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without a configuration-enforced bucket-default encryption setting.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so bucket- or account-level public ACLs and policies are not blocked as defence in depth.
The runbooks bucket, which commonly holds internal operational procedures and infrastructure detail useful to an attacker, has no default server-side encryption configured.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbook content is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection purposes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving no defence-in-depth control against a subsequent public ACL or policy grant on internal operational documentation.

findings.issue_category: invalid canned ACL on log bucket
findings.description: The ACL value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL (it appears to be a corruption of "log-delivery-write"), so the intended access control grant on the audit log destination bucket is not what was intended; the resulting access posture of the central log sink is unpredictable.

force_destroy = true on the central audit log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted in a single operation, and no MFA delete or object lock protects log integrity against tampering by an actor with write access.

The audit log sink has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and it is configured with a delivery-write style ACL; without a public access block there is no backstop preventing public exposure of collected access logs.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded into a bucket with no default encryption and no per-object server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument, so potentially sensitive third-party data is stored without an explicitly enforced encryption setting.
